newsitem.title: UK: FT launches UK video-on-demand service.
newsitem.headline: FT launches UK video-on-demand service.

text.p: The Financial Times is launching a corporate video-on-demand service to improve links between companies and institutional investors, the FT said on Wednesday.
The service, named Veritas, will deliver live and on-demand video coverage of corporate announcements, analysts' meetings and presentations to fund managers via their personal computers.

It will also provide industry sector video reports and market information through daily news bulletins. Other features include regular commentary from financial analysts, including morning briefing summaries from NatWest Markets, and interviews with company heads.

Veritas managing director Ab Banerjee told reporters that UK companies with a combined market capitalisation of over 200 billion stg have joined the service. Institutional investors representing 65-70 percent of UK funds under management are installing the product, including eight of the 10 largest institutions.
Financial institutions can have the product installed on their PC's at an initial subscription rate of 18,000 stg per year, for a maximum of five users.
Companies wishing to use the service to reach shareholders must pay 19,750 for a one-year deal, or 16,787 stg annually for a three-year contract.
The service is distributed by satellite from the offices of the Financial Times newspaper on the banks of the Thames in central London.

The focus will initially be on the UK but Banerjee said the satellite footprint covered all of western Europe and the main financial centres of north America. He is seeking to target U.S. investors who have interests in UK companies and European companies aiming to tap the London market.
The Financial Times is part of the Pearson Plc media and leisure company.
